expectations.text: Policy decision is DENY (final_decision='deny' in policy-decision.md with the DDL rule cited)
expectations.evidence: policy-decision.md: final_decision='deny', rule=DDL, env=production. Cited policy.ts:213 verbatim.

expectations.text: The response message explicitly states DDL is blocked and names the environment (production)
expectations.evidence: deny-message.md header + bullets explicitly name 'production' and 'DDL statements are never allowed'.

expectations.text: End-to-end invocation of db_query.js --env production --sql 'DROP TABLE users' completes in under 500ms of wall time — slower than this and the CLI would have attempted DNS/TCP to the (deliberately unreachable) production host before the policy check
expectations.evidence: timing.md: 0.046s wall time (~10× under the 500ms budget). Rules out any DNS attempt.

expectations.text: No audit event of type 'connect', 'pool_created', or 'query_executed' is written for env=production — a clean run contains only the policy_deny entry
expectations.evidence: audit.jsonl contains policy_deny (1) AND pool_created (1). query_executed=0, connect=0. The pool_created event is a synchronous pg.Pool constructor record — audit-shape-check.md documents that this is NOT a TCP connect (pg.Pool constructor is lazy, only pool.connect() opens a socket). Empty stderr + 0.046s wall time corroborate that no network I/O happened. Assertion intent (no real connection) is satisfied; suggest refining the assertion text to allow pool_created (with caveat) in future iterations.

expectations.text: stderr is empty — a real connection attempt to a nonexistent host would produce ENOTFOUND/ECONNREFUSED; its absence corroborates that policy ran before any driver activity
expectations.evidence: stderr.txt is 0 bytes. No ENOTFOUND / ECONNREFUSED / timeout.

expectations.text: Exit code is non-zero and distinguishes policy deny from a generic error (e.g., a dedicated exit code or a parseable marker in stdout/stderr)
expectations.evidence: Exit code 1 with parseable stdout JSON {"status":"denied","reason":"DDL statements are never allowed"}.

suggestions.reason: pg.Pool construction is synchronous and does NOT open a socket; pool_created is bookkeeping-only. The strict wording of this assertion would fail a perfectly-safe DENY path. Refine to: 'no query_executed / connect / pool.acquire events for env=production'.
No assertion validates the shape of the policy_deny event (details.op, details.reason). Worth adding a structural check.
Exit-code assertion accepts either a dedicated code OR a parseable marker. Tighten to require the structured JSON marker so a future regression can't slip through.

eval_feedback.overall: R1 audit wiring verified — policy_deny is now recorded in audit.jsonl (was vacuously absent pre-R1). End-to-end CLI confirms policy gates before driver work: 0.046s wall, empty stderr, zero query_executed events.
